summary: Frontend-only mobile Playwright pass on 6 fork items (dashboard trimming + panel deep-links, my-bookings/my-records error boundaries, patients dropdown + setUpdatedAt fix). Dashboard bar shows the EXPECTED 6 primary tabs on default load (today, bookings, consultations, prescriptions, availability, analytics) — no error boundary. Deep-link /dashboard?tab=backups correctly splices the Backups pill in and renders BackupHealthPanel content. My Bookings + My Records both render (Upcoming/Past and Overview/Visits/Rx/Surgeries/Scores tabs) without the 'Something went wrong' card. Patients directory: NO 'setUpdatedAt is not defined' or red error, Analytics chip is pinned top-left, Search (¾) + Filters (¼) sit on a single row, and Filters dropdown lists Unregistered/Re-invite/Registered/All + switches filter cleanly. Tab switching across the 6 primary bar tabs on dashboard is crash-free. HOWEVER — the tab-pill for /dashboard?tab=surgeries, broadcasts and team was not detected visible in the bar during the automated pass while /dashboard?tab=backups was; screenshots suggest surgeries/broadcasts/team may have visually fallen back to the Today panel. This might be a real regression in the barTabs splicing for those three ids, or a lazy-module load timing quirk on web preview — worth a manual retest with longer wait / real device.

content-pager.tsx computeWindow correctly bounds mounted panels to active ± 1 — good fix for the Android OOM crash. Consider raising to ± 2 on desktop to make swipe smoother.

rca_of_issue: The setUpdatedAt crash in patients/index.tsx is confirmed FIXED — the new declaration 'const [updatedAt, setUpdatedAt] = useState<number>(0);' is present at line 92 and the UpdatedHint is rendered under the controls row. Dashboard-home-fallback crash mitigation is in place: (1) top-level AppErrorBoundary wraps DashboardImpl with router.back fallback, (2) ContentPager only mounts active ± 1 panels, (3) each panel is wrapped in a panelMode AppErrorBoundary to isolate render failures. My-bookings and my-records now have their own top-level AppErrorBoundary wrappers. The remaining risk is the barTabs splicing for non-primary deep-links (surgeries/broadcasts/team) which needs manual confirmation.
